label: Summary Tile
title: Summary Tile
summary: Use a Summary Tile to head a dashboard block: a title with a confidence meter, one line about the block, and one action or a chevron.
corePrinciple: Name the block, then offer one way in.

anatomy.title: A title, a meter, a line, and an action
anatomy.description: The tile is one row with no panel of its own: the title and its meter sit over a line of description, and the action sits at the end. The chevron, when chevron is on, follows the action.

configuration.title: An action, a chevron, or neither
configuration.description: children holds the action. Left out, the tile shows a placeholder Button with no onPress, so pass your own Button or IconButton, or null for none. The tile passes its modes to whatever you put there, and your Button’s own modes win. Give the tile AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S, as every example here does, and your Button is purple and small, as Figma draws it. chevron adds a forward arrow at the end. AppearanceBrand, Emphasis, and Semantic Intent change only the action: the title, description, and meter keep their look.

states.title: Confidence, and a pressable row
states.description: confidence shows how much data stands behind the block: High lights three green bars, Medium two orange, Low one red, and None, the default, three grey. A number from 0 to 1 picks the nearest level. onPress makes the whole row one button that dims while pressed; it removes the placeholder Button, not one you pass. The tile has no disabled, selected, or loading state.

sizing.title: The host sets the width
sizing.description: The tile fills its host’s width and adds no padding, background, or border: the card or screen around it supplies them. Figma draws it at 280 px. The text takes the room the action leaves, so the description wraps onto more lines, and the title ends in … unless disableTruncation is set. The parts are 8 px apart, and the meter sits 4 px after the title.

content.title: Name the block, say what’s in it, use a verb
content.description: Make the title the block’s name in a word or two, such as Spending, Bills, or Goals. The description says what the block holds in one short line; it never truncates, so a paragraph makes the row tall. Label the action with a verb for the block, such as Set budget, Pay bills, or Add goal.

inContext.title: Spending on the Money screen
inContext.description: The tile heads a card, and the list under it is the block it introduces. See all opens the screen’s own spending view through the Button’s onPress; the tile only lays out the row.

sources.title: Use the public Summary Tile contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (19 October build of Biscuit’s main) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Summary Tile exposes only chevron and the action slot; the title, description, and confidence are overrides there. The package’s default action is a placeholder Button with no onPress, and a Button passed in children doesn’t get its purple, size S look, so these examples set AppearanceBrand Secondary and Button / Size S on the tile. The title’s line is 20 px (Figma 18), so a one-line tile is 44 px tall, not 42. disableTruncation affects only the title, and a tile without onPress isn’t announced by its title. The published Storybook still shows the older generated page (all reported).
